title: Personal details and home address
purpose: Collect the employee's name, date of birth and complete home address once. HR uses them to post documents and the pension fund to register the employee. The country of the address decides which later questions apply, and the canton is asked only of employees living in Switzerland.

stories.title: Collect the employee's name and date of birth
stories.i_want: every new employee to give their first name, last name and date of birth in the onboarding questionnaire
stories.so_that: the employee can be registered for the occupational pension: the registration cannot be submitted without these required fields. HR also uses the name to identify the employee and to address posted documents
stories.priority_reason: First name, last name and date of birth are required fields of the pension fund registration. The registration is rejected without them ('<Field> is required.'), so missing values block it.

acceptance_criteria.title: First and last name are asked of every employee and cannot be left empty
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in the onboarding questionnaire, whatever their country of residence, nationality or civil status
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the personal details
acceptance_criteria.then: the questionnaire asks for the first name and the last name. Both are required, and the questionnaire cannot be submitted while either is empty. The names are recorded for the pension fund registration (its required 'First name' and 'Last name' fields) and for HR, which uses them to identify the employee and address posted documents

acceptance_criteria.title: Date of birth is asked of every employee as a date DD.MM.YYYY
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in the onboarding questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the personal details
acceptance_criteria.then: the questionnaire asks for the employee's date of birth as a date in the form DD.MM.YYYY (e.g. 14.03.1990). It is required, and the questionnaire cannot be submitted without it. The date of birth is recorded for the pension fund registration (its required 'Date of birth' field)

acceptance_criteria.title: Name and date of birth are asked once only
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered their name and date of birth
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee continues through the rest of the questionnaire
acceptance_criteria.then: no later step asks for the employee's own name or date of birth again. The same answers serve both the pension fund and HR

stories.title: Collect a complete postal home address
stories.i_want: every new employee to give their full home address: street, house number, postcode, town and country
stories.so_that: HR can post documents to the employee without chasing missing address parts
stories.priority_reason: HR posts a lot of documents to employees and states that the address 'has to be complete'. An incomplete address blocks posting.

acceptance_criteria.title: All five parts of the home address are asked of every employee and required
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee fills in the onboarding questionnaire, whether they live in Switzerland or abroad
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee reaches the home address
acceptance_criteria.then: the questionnaire asks for the street, house number, postcode, town and country of the home address. All five are required, and the questionnaire cannot be submitted while any part is missing. The address is recorded for HR to post documents

acceptance_criteria.title: The address is a normal postal address, nothing more
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee enters their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire asks for the address
acceptance_criteria.then: it asks only for what is written on an envelope (street, house number, postcode, town, country) and no further address details. Whether every address has a house number is not stated by any source, so the house number stays required as HR listed it

acceptance_criteria.title: The country is named in English
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee enters the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: the employee chooses or states the country
acceptance_criteria.then: the country is recorded by its English name, e.g. "Switzerland", "Germany", "Liechtenstein"

stories.title: Use the home address country as the country of residence
stories.i_want: the country of the employee's home address to serve as their country of residence, without a separate question
stories.so_that: Lonio can tell whether the employee lives in Switzerland or abroad. That decides who is subject to source tax, which follow-up questions apply (nationality, canton, the cross-border questions for Germany and Liechtenstein), and the tariff code Lonio computes
stories.priority_reason: Employees living abroad are always subject to source tax. Without the country of residence neither source tax liability nor the tariff code can be determined, and HR says it never knows up front who has to answer the source tax questions.

acceptance_criteria.title: The country of residence is not asked separately
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee has entered the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire needs the employee's country of residence (for source tax or for the pension fund's canton)
acceptance_criteria.then: it uses the country of the home address and does not ask a separate country-of-residence question

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees living abroad are subject to source tax whatever their nationality
acceptance_criteria.given: the country of the home address is not Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.when: Lonio decides whether the employee is subject to source tax (rule subject_to_source_tax, owned by the source tax section)
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is subject to source tax, and their nationality is not asked. This includes Swiss citizens living abroad (e.g. Stefan) and Liechtenstein residents. Liechtenstein residents are asked the source tax questions, although their result may be 'in principle no source tax liability' (D-007)

acceptance_criteria.title: Employees living in Switzerland get the residence-dependent questions
acceptance_criteria.given: the country of the home address is Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked for the canton (see US-02.4) and for their nationality, which decides source tax liability for residents (owned by another section). The cross-border questions for Germany and Liechtenstein are not asked

acceptance_criteria.title: Germany and Liechtenstein lead to their cross-border questions
acceptance_criteria.given: the country of the home address is Germany or Liechtenstein
acceptance_criteria.then: the employee is asked that country's cross-border questions, starting with whether they return home daily (owned by the source tax section). Employees living in any other country abroad are asked neither set. This follows the calculator's residence options Germany, Liechtenstein and other country

stories.title: Ask Swiss residents for their canton
stories.i_want: employees living in Switzerland to choose their canton from the 26 Swiss cantons
stories.so_that: the required 'Canton' field of the pension fund registration can be filled, while employees abroad are not asked for a canton they do not have
stories.priority_reason: 'Canton' is a required field of the pension fund registration, and the registration is rejected without it ('Canton is required.').

acceptance_criteria.title: The canton is asked and required only of employees living in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: a new employee has entered the country of their home address
acceptance_criteria.when: the questionnaire decides whether to ask for the canton
acceptance_criteria.then: if the country is Switzerland, the canton is asked and required. Otherwise it is not asked. What the fund expects for employees living abroad, and whether 'Canton' means canton of residence or of work, is still open (see OQ-canton-abroad, non-blocking)

acceptance_criteria.title: The canton is one of the fund's 26 Swiss cantons
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee lives in Switzerland and is asked for the canton
acceptance_criteria.then: they choose exactly one of the fund's list: Aargau, Appenzell Ausserrhoden, Appenzell Innerrhoden, Basel-Landschaft, Basel-Stadt, Bern, Fribourg, Geneva, Glarus, Graubünden, Jura, Lucerne, Neuchâtel, Nidwalden, Obwalden, Schaffhausen, Schwyz, Solothurn, St. Gallen, Thurgau, Ticino, Uri, Valais, Vaud, Zug, Zurich. The answer is recorded for the pension fund registration

acceptance_criteria.title: A canton is not kept for an employee who no longer lives in Switzerland
acceptance_criteria.given: the employee chose a canton and then changed the country of the home address from Switzerland to another country before submitting
acceptance_criteria.then: the canton answer is discarded and not recorded, because no party needs it for this employee. Until submission it may be kept, so switching back to Switzerland does not lose the answer

examples.name: Employee corrects the country to Germany
